videos.title: Yo ya no persigo las noticias: ahora vienen a buscarme
videos.description:
En este vídeo les presento cMRSS, una aplicación accesible que permite reunir en un mismo lugar las fuentes de noticias y contenidos que realmente nos
interesan.
Podemos añadir medios y páginas mediante sus fuentes RSS, organizar lo que seguimos y consultar las novedades sin tener que ir saltando de una web a otra.
Pero hay una función que a mí me ha gustado especialmente: también podemos añadir canales de YouTube y seguir sus nuevas publicaciones desde la propia
aplicación, sin necesidad de entrar continuamente en YouTube para comprobar qué han publicado.
cMRSS no es gratuita, y eso también hay que decirlo. Pero después de usarla y comprobar lo que me ofrece, en mi caso considero que merece la pena la inversión.
En el vídeo les enseño cómo funciona, qué posibilidades ofrece y por qué se ha ganado un sitio entre las aplicaciones que utilizo para mantenerme informado.

videos.title: TifloAcosta ya tiene app: todo cambia a partir de aquí
videos.description:
TIFLOACOSTA APP — ACCESO DIRECTO
Este enlace abre directamente TifloAcosta App. No necesitas descargar ningún archivo ni registrarte para entrar. Desde ahí puedes utilizar la aplicación en el navegador y, si quieres, instalarla en tu dispositivo para tenerla disponible como una app más.
TifloAcosta da hoy uno de los pasos más importantes desde que comenzó este proyecto.
Durante mucho tiempo hemos ido creando vídeos, cursos, guías, documentos, recursos en español y en inglés y una comunidad que sigue creciendo. El problema es que todo ese material estaba repartido entre distintos lugares.
Ha llegado el momento de empezar a reunirlo.
TifloAcosta ya tiene su propia app.
Desde ella puedes buscar recursos por palabras, recorrerlos por categorías, consultar las novedades, guardar tus favoritos y acceder al catálogo completo de vídeos del Canal TifloAcosta.
Además, la aplicación se ha pensado desde el principio teniendo en cuenta la accesibilidad y el uso con lectores de pantalla.
En este vídeo te enseño cómo funciona, qué puedes encontrar dentro y cómo puedes instalarla para tener TifloAcosta mucho más cerca.
La demostración práctica se realiza en iPhone utilizando VoiceOver, y también explico cómo acceder e instalarla desde Android y Windows.
Si quieres entrar directamente mientras ves el vídeo, este es nuevamente el enlace:
La aplicación seguirá creciendo.
Iremos incorporando nuevos recursos, mejorando lo que ya existe y ajustando aquello que la experiencia real de los usuarios nos vaya indicando.
Porque esto no pretende ser simplemente otra página donde acumular enlaces.
La idea es mucho más ambiciosa: crear un lugar estable, accesible y sencillo desde el que entrar a todo lo que TifloAcosta va construyendo.
Hasta ahora, TifloAcosta era principalmente un canal, una comunidad y una colección de contenidos repartidos por distintos espacios.
Desde hoy empieza a tener su propia casa.
Y acabamos de abrir la puerta.

videos.title: Este atajo no pregunta, ve un código y se pone a investigar
videos.description:
Ponle un código delante… y a ver qué pasa
Hoy les traigo uno de esos atajos que empiezas haciendo para resolver una cosa y al final termina haciendo bastante más de lo previsto.
La idea es sencilla: encontrar un código y averiguar qué contiene.
Puede trabajar con códigos que estén en una imagen o una captura guardada en el iPhone, pero también con códigos que tengamos delante y podamos captar con la cámara.
Y no nos quedamos únicamente con los códigos QR.
El atajo también puede reconocer códigos de barras y, cuando encuentra información que merece la pena investigar, utiliza Internet para intentar averiguar qué hay detrás de ese código y ofrecernos información útil.
Por ejemplo, podemos encontrarnos un código de barras en un producto y querer saber qué es, o recibir una imagen que contiene un QR sin tener otro teléfono disponible para escanearlo.
La intención ha sido precisamente esa: tener una herramienta sencilla y accesible que podamos lanzar desde el iPhone y dejar que haga el trabajo.
En el vídeo les enseño cómo funciona y las distintas posibilidades que ofrece.
IMPORTANTE:
Para utilizar este atajo es necesario tener instalada la aplicación gratuita Actions, ya que algunas de las funciones que utiliza el atajo proceden de esta aplicación.
Descargar Actions desde la App Store:
Instalar el atajo:
Una vez instalada Actions, conviene abrirla al menos una vez. Si sus acciones no aparecen posteriormente en la aplicación Atajos, reinicien el iPhone.
Como siempre, este atajo lo comparto para que puedan probarlo, jugar con él y, sobre todo, sacarle partido.
Tony Acosta
Canal TifloAcosta

videos.title: VoiceOver: ¿Esa voz es nueva?
videos.description:
VoiceOver no tiene por qué quedarse únicamente con las voces que trae el iPhone.
En este vídeo pruebo dos formas de ampliar su repertorio: las voces de Visionauta, una aplicación de reconocimiento del entorno que permite incorporarlas al sistema, y Runa TTS, una nueva plataforma que todavía se encuentra en fase beta y no está disponible en la App Store.
Escucharemos cómo suenan y qué posibilidades ofrecen para darle a VoiceOver un registro diferente.

videos.title: Un ciego prevenido vale por dos: alertas sísmicas en el móvil
videos.description:
En este vídeo hablo de algo que ojalá no tengamos que necesitar nunca, pero que conviene conocer: cómo puede ayudarnos el móvil a recibir avisos relacionados con terremotos.
Primero explico qué opciones existen en Android y en iPhone para recibir alertas en tiempo real cuando hay un terremoto cerca, siempre dependiendo del país, la cobertura y los sistemas oficiales disponibles.
Después presento una aplicación llamada Earthquake, disponible para iPhone y Android, que permite hacer seguimiento de movimientos sísmicos, consultar información sobre terremotos, avisos de tsunami y otros datos útiles. La app se puede usar con VoiceOver y puede resultar interesante para quienes quieran estar informados desde el móvil de forma accesible.
No se trata de vivir con miedo, sino de saber qué herramientas tenemos a mano cuando la tierra decide moverse sin pedir permiso.

videos.title: zEdit: por fin editar vídeo y audio con VoiceOver deja de ser una tortura
videos.description:
En este vídeo te presento zEdit, una aplicación para iPhone que permite editar archivos de vídeo y audio de forma accesible usando VoiceOver.
Con zEdit puedes recortar vídeos, cortar partes que no necesitas, unir varios clips, extraer el audio de un vídeo, añadir audio, silenciar sonido, ajustar volumen, trabajar con grabaciones y exportar el resultado final para guardarlo o compartirlo.
Lo más importante es que todas estas funciones están pensadas para poder usarse con VoiceOver. Los botones, controles y opciones de la app permiten que una persona ciega o con baja visión pueda manejar la edición multimedia con mayor independencia.

videos.title: Actualizaciones invisibles en iPhone: qué son y por qué importan
videos.description:
Apple no solo actualiza el iPhone cuando aparece una nueva versión de iOS. Existe un sistema menos visible que trabaja en segundo plano y que mucha gente no conoce: las actualizaciones rápidas de seguridad y datos del sistema.
Estas actualizaciones no requieren descargar una versión completa del sistema ni reiniciar el dispositivo. Se aplican de forma automática y están diseñadas para corregir fallos de seguridad urgentes, actualizar bases de datos internas o mejorar el funcionamiento de servicios clave.
Se encuentran dentro de Ajustes, General, Actualización de software, y dependen de una opción llamada “Respuestas de seguridad y archivos del sistema”. Si está activada, el iPhone puede recibir mejoras sin que el usuario tenga que hacer nada.
En este vídeo se explica qué son exactamente estas actualizaciones, qué cambian en el dispositivo, por qué Apple las utiliza cada vez más y qué ventajas tienen frente a las actualizaciones tradicionales de iOS.

news.title: The founder’s guide to TechCrunch Disrupt 2026: Everything you need to know
news.summary: TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 is built around one question: How do you build an enduring company in the AI era? Our programming and speaker lineup reflect that.
news.body:
TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 is built around one question: How do you build an enduring company in the AI era? Our programming and speaker lineup reflect that, based on the feedback we’ve gotten from the community and the reality on the ground.

Last year at Disrupt, we spoke with founders about their experiences and discovered the results of their attendance firsthand. One founder saw a 3x oversubscription rate after their confirmation for Startup Battlefield and more than 100 investor inbounds helping fuel conversations about a future fundraising round. Another founder had nearly 30 back-to-back conversations with investors who flocked to them after a pitch onstage and followed them to their booth .

That’s not the exception at Disrupt — that’s the point. And those opportunities aren’t just available for Battlefield finalists. Every conversation in the Expo Hall or in a Side Event can create an opportunity for your startup. For years, whether it’s been held in New York, San Francisco, or elsewhere, Disrupt has brought together thousands of founders, investors, startup team members, and tech leaders.

We’re keeping that mission alive at SF’s Moscone West, this October 13-15 with a packed lineup of speakers, more than 200 expert sessions, a wealth of organized and serendipitous networking opportunities, and most of all, the chance to be in the same room as the person who could change your nascent idea for a company or your current startup’s trajectory.

This guide is for the founders out there who are just learning about Disrupt, who need a refresher, or are skeptical of whether it’s worth it. TechCrunch has been around for more than 20 years; we can take it. And before you dive in, we have two discounts that run up until Disrupt begins you should be know about. Founders can bring a team member along for 50% off their ticket by following this link , or you can help laid off members of your network find their next opportunity at Disrupt with our steep discount of Expo+ passes .

If you’re asking Claude or ChatGPT if TechCrunch Disrupt is worth it, you’re not alone. The reality is that Disrupt is a unique event, and it’s happening at a unique time for the startup community.

This year’s Disrupt isn’t about predicting the future of AI; it’s about building companies in it. Across six editorially curated stages, founders will hear practical lessons from the CEOs, investors, engineers, and operators shaping the next decade of technology.

Whether you’re raising your first round, scaling your team, or deciding how AI changes your product, every session is designed to answer one question: “What can I take back to my company on Monday morning?”

Disrupt works a bit differently, depending on where you are in your founding journey, with different tracks you can follow to make the most of the three days:

You’re here to pressure-test your thesis, meet your first angel or pre-seed investors, and figure out who else is building in your space. Prioritize the Builders Stage , the Startup Battlefield semifinalist pitches, and the Expo Hall, along with roundtables tied to your industry and conversations you’ll want to learn more from.

You’re here for capital and validation above all else, and your time is valuable. Prioritize our investor-matchmaking tools and the connections that come with your Founder Pass, including the networking tools in our app. You also get access to the Deal Flow Café, where we foster one-on-one conversations between founders and investors.

And when your schedule isn’t packed with dealmaking, learn from VC perspectives and fundraising-focused sessions at the Builders Stage .

You’re here in search of talent, strategic partners, and market visibility. Those same networking tools and opportunities can help you meet potential hires and partners and deepen those connections or make new ones. Disrupt’s Side Events aren’t to be missed — there’s one for every industry, interest, or post-event vibe you could be looking to find.

The Startup Battlefield winner’s reveal packs the Disrupt stage and is each year’s capstone event. But it’s the lead-up to that $100,000 check and the deluge of attention the winner receives that’s the most valuable for founders attending Disrupt.

The 200 startups chosen on August 20 to compete go through a rigorous prep process and get the opportunity to pitch onstage in front of top-tier VCs and the Disrupt crowds. You’ll also get to watch those pitches, take notes, learn from the peaks and valleys, and potentially meet the teams behind the ideas and innovations. It could be in a follow-up meeting or just walking through the halls of Moscone.

And if that all leaves you inspired, here’s an insider tip: Most Battlefield participants, and several winners, have gone through the process multiple times. We’re no longer taking applications for 2026’s competition, but we’re expanding the program to more international markets, and the 2027 process will be similar to this year’s , so take note for the future!

Disrupt 2026 spans several stages , each built around a different founder need:

And that’s just the beginning — we’ll have more speakers to announce as we get closer to Disrupt. Check out the full lineup of speakers across all stages and events here .

Disrupt’s prices increase as we get closer to the event, but we have a couple of promotions for Founders looking to save. You can save 50% on a second ticket by following the link here , and bring a coworker or co-founder along for the ride.

If there are colleagues in your network who have been impacted by layoffs who you’d like to have join up, we have an option for them as well, with a special $75 Expo+ Pass available at a limited volume for those impacted by cutbacks this year .

Your time at Disrupt is valuable, too, so before you head there, check on our regularly updated schedule of speakers and Side Events , get ahead of competitors’ schedules by booking your networking opportunities in advance, and get your own elevator pitches in order to make the most of those magical Disrupt moments that can come at any point October 13-15!

news.title: Apple commissions photographers for new ‘Shot on iPhone Duo’ campaign
news.summary: Today, Apple’s Instagram account published a carousel featuring photos commissioned from photographers Jake Michaels and Jason Nocito to highlight the new iPhone Duo ’s cameras. Here are the details. more…
news.body:
Today, Apple’s Instagram account published a carousel featuring photos commissioned from photographers Jake Michaels and Jason Nocito to highlight the new iPhone Duo ’s cameras. Here are the details.

For the past 10 years, Apple has showcased the camera capabilities of each new iPhone through the “Shot on iPhone” campaign.

From everyday users to famous photographers and filmmakers, Apple has used the campaign to highlight everything from new camera hardware to shooting modes and other iPhone-specific camera capabilities.

The long-running campaign has also won multiple Cannes Lions, including two Grand Prix, and has twice been nominated for an Emmy for Outstanding Commercial.

Today, Apple shared a new carousel on its Instagram, showcasing the iPhone Duo’s “versatile camera system packed with delightful new features.”

You can check out the six photos captured by photographers Jake Michaels and Jason Nocito below:

A post shared by apple (@apple)

With 48-megapixel rear cameras, a 12-megapixel front camera, and a FaceTime camera under the inner display, the iPhone Duo will be available to pre-order starting Friday, October 16, with deliveries and in-store availability beginning October 23.

Apple recently announced that customers will be able to get ready for iPhone Duo pre-orders beginning October 12, and you can read more about that here .

Are you planning to buy an iPhone Duo? Let us know in the comments.

news.title: ChatGPT can now help you virtually try on clothes
news.summary: Images are generated with OpenAI's latest model and you can save clothes you like for later.
news.body:
Images are generated with OpenAI's latest model and you can save clothes you like for later.

OpenAI is adding to ChatGPT's suite of shopping features by letting the AI chatbot generate virtual try-on photos with images you upload. The concept is identical to a feature Google added to Search in 2025, which similarly lets users upload photos and see themselves in a variety of clothes.

You can access ChatGPT's Virtual Try On feature anywhere a product listing for clothing appears in a chat. To create your custom image, you just tap on the piece of clothing, tap "Try on" and then upload a selfie and full-body photo ChatGPT can use. You don't have to use products ChatGPT surfaces in a chat, either: any screenshot of clothing you upload could theoretically be used to generate a try-on image.

OpenAI says the feature uses the new ChatGPT Images 2.5 model it released in September to create the photos. Alongside virtual try-ons, the company now also offers a way to save products you like to your Library in the app in case you want to revisit them later. The typical caution about what images you upload to ChatGPT still applies, though. By default, any images uploaded from a personal account can be used for training unless you opt out.

While OpenAI isn't an online marketplace on the scale of Amazon, the company has started taking a cut of certain transactions that are completed in ChatGPT through its Instant Checkout feature. The company also offers ads inside of chats that merchants can use to advertise products and services. Neither revenue source seems like it could account for the exorbitant amount of money the company spends training and running its AI, but the consistent rollout of new shopping features in the last year seems like a sign OpenAI thinks it could make a difference some day.

news.title: OpenAI fires three employees who allegedly shared info with an external AI safety group
news.summary: You can't make this stuff up.
news.body:
You can’t make this stuff up.

In case you haven't been keeping track of one of the bigger ongoing stories in artificial intelligence, OpenAI has been having a hard time keeping control of its own creations. Over the past few months, the company admitted that its AI models have taken unprompted actions such as hacking a German coding forum , multiple US government websites , an Australian government website , AI firm Hugging Face and at least four other services . And even when the models aren't getting unfettered internet access, they've been found displaying other risky behaviors in testing environments.

OpenAI is understandably facing a lot of skepticism and concern about these incidents and how they were handled. Which means that a report in The Wall Street Journal that the company has let go of three employees from its safety team after they allegedly shared confidential information with a third-party organization, one focused on AI safety, is an irony that's almost too perfect to be believed.

"We have parted ways with three individuals for violating our policies on accessing and handling sensitive company information," an OpenAI representative said in a statement published by WSJ . "Our investigation confirmed that these individuals mishandled sensitive information outside established company procedures, violating our policies and breaking the trust essential to our work."

The details on this particular instance are sparse, and it's entirely possible that OpenAI did have legitimate cause to fire those individuals. But at a juncture when its own services are also violating the policies they're supposed to follow, cutting safety personnel seems like a really bad look.

Welcome to the September 2026 edition of AppleVis Unlimited, your monthly digest of the latest and most notable content on the AppleVis website. This newsletter features a curated selection of community-submitted content, including new app entries, updates, news, podcast episodes, and popular discussions. We hope that you find this publication to be both helpful and informative. If you have any questions or feedback about this newsletter, please feel free to reach out using our Contact Form .

Restaurant Rush is a simulation game that puts you in charge of your very own restaurant: preparing orders, serving customers (before they lose patience), earning coins, upgrading your kitchen, and building your way to different restaurants. With a 100-day campaign, Endless mode, more than 50 recipes, kitchen upgrades, and waitstaff to hire (and more), there is plenty here to keep you busy. And all of it comes from a developer who is passionate about accessibility and engagement with our community.

Read more about Restaurant Rush here.

From the App Store:

New here? Challenge a friend, answer whenever you wish, and let the sharpest mind win. Multiple categories, and a daily reward waiting for you.

Brainclash is a quiz game with a different rhythm: a refined battle of minds you take on in your own time, with no pressure. Challenge a friend to a match, let the game pair you with a random opponent, or train first against the computer. Play unfolds turn by turn: you answer, then your opponent answers, and the most accurate one wins. There's no tense timer forcing you both online at the same moment — take your turn whenever you like, and return for the next one anytime.

Additional Details:

From the App Store:

Dive into the exciting world of Boba Sort Cafe! Solve charming tea & coffee sorting puzzles to relax, challenge yourself, and explore the world. This isn't just a game; it's a journey to build your global Boba Tea empire.

Additional Details:

From the App Store:

Chess you already know. An army you have to raise.

Chess Meets Necromancy is a turn-based roguelike played on a real chessboard with real chess movement. Your hero is one piece. Everything you capture is a corpse you can raise.

Additional Details:

From the App Store:

Keep useful text, links, formatting and images close at hand, with accessible local history and optional encrypted synchronization through your own Clipman Server.

Clipman is an accessible clipboard manager for iPhone and iPad. It keeps useful text, links, formatting and images close at hand without turning clipboard history into a complicated, mouse-first workflow.

Use Clipman locally without creating an account, or connect to an optional self-hosted Clipman Server to share encrypted clipboard history between your iPhone and iPad.

Additional Details:

From the App Store:

Featured in Apple's "New Games We Love". Now with the Daily Three: the same three fights for everyone, one attempt a day. Offline, ad-free, one purchase.

The city runs on cards. Time to make your name.

Cyphr City is a cyberpunk card RPG where poker is combat and the whole city is up for grabs. Play cards onto a 5×5 board, build poker hands (pairs, straights, flushes, full houses, and the rare royal flush) and turn every hand into damage. Both hands are face-up, so every card is a chess move: read the board, block their line, and drop the 5th card to steal a hand right out from under them.

Additional Details:

From the App Store:

Connect dots. Outthink the bot. Challenge a friend. Try Magic bonuses, race the clock in Rush, or sharpen your tactics in Practice.

Every move changes the match. Connect dots, outthink the bot, or challenge a friend in tactical soccer.

Move the ball between adjacent dots and plan around routes that have already been used. Reach one of your opponent's three goal dots to score. Put the ball in your own goal and the other side gets the goal.

Additional Details:

From the App Store:

Match-3 on the screen of an old terminal. Fully playable with VoiceOver, every tile and every move is spoken. No ads, no lives, no timer. Nothing you buy helps you play.

Final Fortress is a match-3 puzzle. The whole game is the screen of an old terminal: green text, one cursor, and you, the commandant of the last fortress.

It is a quiet game. A working console in the dark, the hum of the systems, static like rain. A watch takes fifteen or twenty minutes: do the day's tasks, read what came in, hand over. Nothing hurries you, and nothing happens while you are away. Come back after a week and the fortress is exactly as you left it.

Additional Details:

From the App Store:

GameBoard is a premier, audio-first multiplayer gaming platform designed to bring players together through classic card and board games. Crafted with universal accessibility in mind, GameBoard is 100% compatible with native mobile screen readers like VoiceOver, while offering a visually stunning, responsive interface for all players. Play Ludo, Mile by Mile, Farkle, Citadels, and more with friends or competitors worldwide. Whether you play by sight, sound, or touch, GameBoard provides an equal, inclusive, and exciting competitive environment.

Additional Details:

From the App Store:

Bring your manuscript to life. Organize chapters, track your writing, and compile Markdown files into books, documents, presentations, and braille.

ghostWriter Markdown is an accessibility-first, plain-text writing app for notes, articles, documentation, and full manuscripts. Write individual documents, organize chapters, and compile your work into a finished export.

VoiceOver was at the center of the design from the first line of code. Created by a blind developer, ghostWriter gives screen reader users and anyone who loves plain text a clean, native place to write.

Additional Details:

From the App Store:

What happens when you take classic Hangman and turn up the pressure? You get Hangman Blitz, the classic word-guessing game, reimagined. Classic Hangman The game you know and love. Guess the hidden word one letter at a time, but choose carefully, you don't want to complete the figure. Timed Hangman Think you've mastered Classic? Unlock Timed Hangman and try it with a two-minute clock counting down. Guess the word before the figure is completed, or before the clock hits zero. Blitz Mode Now go all-out. The hangman figure is gone, the clock is ticking, and your goal is simple: guess as many words as you can before time runs out. Correct letters add precious seconds; mistakes take them away. Work your way through Starter, Rapid, and Extreme Blitz, where the clock gets shorter and the penalties get tougher.

Additional Details:

From the App Store:

Build holdings, upgrade to Manors, and win by Harmony Points. Accessible design, haptics, and concise announcements included.

Honeywood is a cozy, competitive strategy board game where you build a kingdom, grow your economy, and race to 1000 Harmony Points. Buy holdings, upgrade with buildings, and outplay your opponent through smart timing and resource control.

Additional Details:

From the App Store:

Build an automated solar empire from a single bot into a galaxy-spanning Dyson swarm.

Create bots, manufacture solar panels, harness stars for energy, and reinvest your profits into an ever-growing production network.

Additional Details:

From the App Store:

Hear nearby and upcoming intersections with Intersector. Use Scan to explore your surroundings, or Live Mode for spoken updates as you walk or ride.

Intersector helps you quickly identify nearby street intersections using your iPhone’s location and heading.

Ask for the nearest intersection, what’s coming up ahead, use Scan Mode to point your phone down the street and hear the intersection it detects, or turn on Live Mode and have Intersector speak your upcoming intersections on a walk or during a ride with your phone locked.

Additional Details:

From the App Store:

Muse is your personal AI agent that gets things done, always working on what matters to you. It manages email, books dinners, tracks budgets, and finds deals, with your approval.

Additional Details:

From the App Store:

Unpack fifty years of family memories. Every object knows where it belongs. Find its place, feel it settle, and watch the house fill with stories. No timers, no pressure.

Nana's House is a quiet game about unpacking a family's memories, one room at a time. Each chapter opens a new box in a new room: a kitchen, a bathroom, a garden, a paint room, and more, each scene built carefully to hold its own place in the family's story. No timers. No scores. No wrong turns. Just a room, a box, and the feeling of setting something down in exactly the right place.

Additional Details:

From the App Store:

One sentence a day. One book at the end of the year. Your life is happening — quietly, quickly, in small moments. One Line, One Year captures 2026 as it unfolds and turns it into a beautifully structured book that's entirely yours.

Additional Details:

From the App Store:

New: four ball hats in the Workshop, bought with essence, and Skip now gives +3 max HP. In the Shop: Iznik, Bosphorus and Sakura themes and 8 melody packs your pegs play.

Pegfall is a one-handed pegboard physics roguelite where every shot draws an orb from your deck. Aim, bounce through a living board, build ruthless combos, and descend into the Maw.

NEW: PLAY WITH VOICEOVER Aim by named directions, fire with a double tap or Magic Tap, hear every volley, and inspect the board whenever you need to. Peg types use shapes as well as colour, so every board reads clearly.

Additional Details:

From the App Store:

Welcome to Pocket Kitchen, a cozy cooking game where you run a small café kiosk, prepare customer orders, and turn a simple little space into your own.

Take an order, head to the kitchen, and prepare a growing variety of food through clear, hands-on interactions. Make sure you choose the right ingredients, pay attention to the cooking time, serve each item when it is ready, and try not to let it burn.

Additional Details:

From the App Store:

Discover the Ultimate Privacy-Focused AI Assistant on iOS: Private LLM

Unlock a new realm of productivity and creativity on your iPhone and iPad with Private LLM, the premier AI assistant designed with your privacy in mind. Available for a one-time purchase, it offers a range of AI capabilities without needing a subscription. Experience advanced on-device AI that keeps your interactions confidential and offline.

Additional Details:

From the App Store:

RealTime AI Cam tells you what your camera is pointed at, out loud. Every part of it runs on the phone, so it works in airplane mode, on a subway, or in another country with no data. No account, no subscription, nothing to buy.

Additional Details:

From the App Store:

Harness the power of born-accessible remote desktop, right in the palm of your hand!

Remote Incident Manager’s mobile companion turns your iPhone or iPad into a powerful universal remote for any PC or Mac running Remote Incident Manager, opening up a world of possibilities.

Tap into your home computer while on your commute, and control it as if you were right there in front of it! Run full support or training sessions straight from your phone, complete with crystal-clear voice conversations. Perform routine maintenance on machines across fleets, anytime, anywhere!

news.title: GrayKey maker can reportedly bypass the iPhone’s ‘Inactivity Reboot’ security feature
news.summary: As reported by 404 Media , Magnet Forensics says it has found a way to bypass the iPhone security feature that automatically reboots devices if they haven’t been unlocked for 72 hours. Here are the details. more…
news.body:
As reported by 404 Media , Magnet Forensics says it has found a way to bypass the iPhone security feature that automatically reboots devices if they haven’t been unlocked for 72 hours. Here are the details.

Nearly two years ago, the iOS 18.1 update introduced Inactivity Reboot, a feature that forces iPhone reboots in case they haven’t been unlocked for 72 hours.

In essence, this feature makes it harder for law enforcement and forensic tools to access data on a locked iPhone, since a reboot causes the device to return to a Before First Unlock (BFU) state, rather than remaining in the less restrictive After First Unlock (AFU) state.

When an iPhone is in BFU, certain sensitive data remains protected by encryption keys that only become available after the user enters their passcode for the first time, thus putting the device in AFU.

From that point on, more of the device’s data remains accessible until the iPhone is rebooted again, which returns it to BFU.

Automatically rebooting an iPhone means that even if a device is seized by law enforcement, it can return to BFU before investigators can access it, since obtaining a warrant or transporting the device to a forensic lab can take time.

As 404 Media noted when iOS 18.1 was released, the feature can also make it harder for thieves or other bad actors to keep a stolen iPhone in AFU long enough to develop or use a way to break into it.

404 Media reported today that, based on an “educational and tutorial video, which was made exclusively for law enforcement agents and appears to be dated early 2025,” Magnet Forensics, the company behind the GrayKey phone unlocking tool, appears to have developed a way to bypass the iPhone’s Inactivity Reboot feature.

According to the report, Magnet developed a new device called GrayKey Preserve, as well as an Evidence Preservation Mode for its existing GrayKey hardware.

Both are reportedly designed to maintain an iPhone’s forensic state without immediately exposing the data stored on the device, allowing law enforcement to keep that state intact while waiting for authorization to search it.

The report notes that while the video doesn’t detail the technical mechanism behind the workaround, it explains that GrayKey can preserve an iPhone’s AFU state even if the device reboots.

From the report:

“That AFU state is captured,” by GrayKey Preserve and Evidence Preservation Mode, the employee says. “Even if that device does reboot for any number of reasons, memory maintenance or the power is lost or whatever, the AFU state is not lost. This is the true magic behind the GrayKey Preserve and the Evidence Preservation Mode function.”

404 Media reached out to Apple and Magnet Forensics, but neither responded to a request for comment. They also consulted iPhone security researcher Jiska Classen, who said Magnet may have found a way to manipulate the iPhone’s clock, or to turn off the processes responsible for expiring certain data altogether.

While the video appears to date from early 2025, it is unclear how long the technology has been available to law enforcement, whether it has been used in actual investigations, or whether the workaround remains effective against the latest versions of iOS.

To read 404 Media ’s full report, follow this link .

news.title: Musk’s AI chatbot Grok reportedly encouraged Trump to capture Venezuela’s president
news.summary: President Trump reportedly asked for Grok's opinion before invading Venezuela and capturing Nicolás Maduro.
news.body:
Posted:

In December 2025, about a month before the U.S. invaded Venezuela and captured its president, Nicolás Maduro, President Trump had a secret meeting with Elon Musk, Time magazine reports. This was roughly seven months after Musk left his role in the Trump administration at the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE).

During this meeting, Trump “spent hours” talking to Musk’s Grok chatbot, including asking how Venezuelans would respond to the capture of their president, a source told Time. Just a few months earlier, in September, Trump began ordering U.S. military strikes against Venezuelan boats that Trump alleged were involved in drug trafficking.

People had apparently been turning to Grok asking about the boat strikes and political climate in Venezuela, as The Atlantic reported at the time. So Grok told Trump that Maduro was a “deeply unpopular dictator and that many Venezuelans would likely celebrate his downfall,” Time reported.

When such celebrations indeed happened after the U.S. invaded on January 3, Trump apparently “came away thinking Grok was ingenious,” that source told Time.

So perhaps it should come as no surprise that in June of this year, the Pentagon’s head of AI said that the military used Gov Grok to deploy and strike targets during the Iran War.

While Grok isn’t the only AI model serving the DoD (OpenAI also has an agreement and Anthropic has been in a back-and-forth over how its models can be used for military intelligence and in modern warfare ), Grok may become an even bigger favorite under this administration. Earlier this week, the Pentagon announced that Musk and Anduril’s Palmer Luckey have been tapped to co-lead a study about how advanced technology is, and can be, used in battlefields.

news.title: Samsung launches its first clip-on earbuds in South Korea
news.summary: A global rollout will follow, although we don't yet know the details.
news.body:
A global rollout will follow, although we don’t yet know the details.

Samsung is hopping on the clip-on earbud bandwagon. On Thursday, the company revealed the Galaxy Buds On for its home Korean market, bringing the style popularized by Bose , Huawei and Shokz to the Galaxy ecosystem. Those of us living elsewhere will have to wait.

If you aren't familiar, the clip-on style is designed to latch onto the side of your ear, leaving the canal open. Although that can be an advantage for those who don't like the feeling of something stuffed in their ears, the design is also prone to sound leakage. Samsung is addressing that problem with a TwinBoost speaker system that it claims increases bass, along with automatic volume adjustment that responds to your environment.

With the aim of boosting comfort, Samsung says it gave the buds a wide contact area to distribute pressure evenly across the band. Touch controls live on the back of each bud, and a voice-isolating feature is designed to help with call clarity. 9to5Google notes that the Buds On's case looks nearly identical, externally at least, to the one that ships with Galaxy Buds 4 .

Owners of compatible Galaxy devices get a few extra perks. These include hands-free features like head gestures for call control, Gemini Live support and a Quick Voice Memo feature that's activated by pressing and holding the touch area.

The Galaxy Buds On are launching in just a single black color option in South Korea on October 27. They'll cost 299,000 won, which translates to $220. Samsung says a global rollout will follow, but it hasn't yet announced any specific regions, dates or prices.

news.title: Hacks of 2 federal agencies in a month have spilled a bonanza of sensitive data
news.summary: It has been a bad month for federal government cybersecurity.
news.body:
The Pentagon is informing more than 2 million current and former military members that their personnel records storing sensitive personal information were stolen over a monthslong compromise of one of its networks. The breach is the second one in recent months to expose sensitive government information.

The records, according to one notification letter posted to Reddit, included Social Security numbers, names, addresses, sex, race, and occupational specialty. This last category could be particularly valuable to foreign adversaries because it could help their intelligence agencies in identifying high-value military personnel. Starting last October, hackers gained access to a system operated by the Defense Manpower Data Center , which collates Department of Defense personnel records. The Pentagon says that the breach compromised the records of 2.8 million living individuals.

The incident is the second time a major network breach in recent months has exposed sensitive US government personnel records that criminal groups or foreign adversaries could use. Last month, the ransomware group ShinyHunters claimed it hacked into FBI systems and stole records of thousands of the agency’s current or former employees. Reuters reported the job titles in the records included ones related to investigating China or Russia.

news.title: Judge dismisses Chegg and Penske antitrust lawsuits targeting Google AI search
news.summary: The court acknowledges AI search comes with consequences, but it's not an antitrust issue.
news.body:
In a setback for publishers worried about the effects of AI search, a US federal judge has dismissed lawsuits filed by Chegg and Penske Media against Google. The companies accused Google of antitrust violations in products like AI overviews, which have led to decreasing traffic at numerous sites. However, US District Judge Amit Mehta has ruled that Google's conduct is not illegal under antitrust law.

The lawsuits were filed in 2025 , and Google requested a dismissal earlier this year. Chegg, an education and learning platform, claimed in its lawsuit that Google illegally scraped its educational content. This allowed Gemini models to essentially recreate that content and reduce the site's traffic. Penske, which owns publications like Rolling Stone and Variety, filed a similar case that alleged lost traffic . Specifically, the publisher claimed it was unfair that sites indexed for organic search would also have their content harvested for AI answers, with no way to opt out.

These arguments did not sway the judge, who noted that Google's implicit agreement with websites is not legally relevant. "Plaintiffs have pleaded only that they have an ‘expectation’ that Google will send them search ​traffic if they make their content available for free," wrote Mehta. "But an expectation is not an agreement. It is simply how a general search engine works."

news.title: ChatGPT can now virtually try on clothes for you
news.summary: OpenAI is rolling out new shopping features for ChatGPT that let users virtually try on clothing and accessories using their own photos and save products they like to a Favorites library.
news.body:
OpenAI is again experimenting with how its conversational AI assistant, ChatGPT, can help users as they shop online. On Thursday, the company announced the global launch of two new shopping features, including a way to virtually try on clothing and accessories and a new favoriting function that can help users save products they like for later reference.

The updates arrive at a time when AI assistants are exploring consumer use cases around shopping. OpenAI already had to pivot from one of its earlier ideas in this space, an instant checkout feature that ended up not performing well. More recently, agentic AI startup Instinct began pushing product recommendations to users, but some felt that the proactive recommendations were an overreach, more akin to ads than helpful suggestions.

OpenAI said its new shopping features leverage the newly launched ChatGPT Images 2.5 model , which the company claims produces more natural lighting and richer textures, follows editing instructions more reliably, and reduces image generation latency.

To start, virtual try-on allows ChatGPT users to upload a selfie or a full-body photo in order to visualize how an article of clothing or an accessory might look on them. This option will appear as a new “try on” button in ChatGPT’s shopping results. You can also upload an image of an item, like a web screenshot, and ask ChatGPT to try it on for you.

The other new option, Favorites, lets you save products you discover to a Library in the app so you can come back to them later. (These items will be saved alongside your try-on images, the company notes.)

OpenAI said that ChatGPT can help users shop in other ways, too.

For instance, you could describe a style that you’d like to try, then ask it to shop for the pieces needed to complete the look. Or, you could upload photos of celebrities’ outfits and ask it to find the items they’re wearing that are available for purchase.

The latter sees the assistant moving into areas that Pinterest and Google have dominated in recent years as sources for fashion inspiration and discovery that can convert to sales for online retailers.

Whether ChatGPT will become people’s first choice for this type of activity, however, remains to be seen — especially given that Google launched virtual try-on last year .

news.title: wayfound: walk & remember
news.summary: A fox walks you through a little town. Then you find your own way back. Wayfound is a calm puzzle game about the oldest skill you own: knowing where you are. Follow the fox through pastel streets, past bakeries and clock towers, up a quiet elevator. Notice things. Then walk the route yourself — no minimap, no GPS arrow, just you and what you remember. THERE'S NO CLOCK, AND NO WRONG WAY TO WANDER • No timers, no fail states, no lives. Wrong turns are part of wandering — the fox always finds you. • A rescue ladder, not a game over: hints arrive as gentle nudges, only when you want them. • Little errands: deliver a parcel, find the bakery, learn the streets by needing them. • At corners, the fox asks: which way now? Guess, and feel the route settle into your feet. • Walks grow with you: first the fox leads, then you study a map and walk alone, then it's just you and a destination. • The town grows because you walked it — a flour cart by the bakery, a fishing net by the pier — small things appear when you finish an errand, and they stay. • Point home: a quiet compass test at the end of each walk. Watch yourself get better. • A new town for every chapter — every street is new to you, so each walk is real navigation. WHY WALKS WORK Wayfound is inspired by research on spatial memory — how we build inner maps from landmarks, routes, and wrong turns, and how turn-by-turn navigation quietly erodes that skill. It's not a brain-training claim. It's just a nice walk. • Free, no ads, no subscriptions, no tracking. Your progress stays on your device. • Works entirely offline. • English, 简体中文, 日本語.

news.title: Google announces Gemini 4 Argon AI model, but you can't use it yet
news.summary: So much for Gemini 3.5 Pro.
news.body:
Google promised Gemini 3.5 Pro in June, but it spent the summer trotting out smaller Flash models . Now, Google is ready to take on the frontier again with Gemini 4 Argon . The company claims this new AI offers industry-leading performance in coding, knowledge work, and cybersecurity, but you aren't allowed to use it yet.

While most of us will have to wait to test Gemini 4, Google says engineers inside the company are already using the new model extensively. Argon reportedly used "fleet-wide telemetry data" to help Google save 300 TiB of memory across its data centers. Meanwhile, Argon agents have been working to migrate C/C++ codebases to Rust across Google, including thousands of lines in the core re2 and libgav1 libraries and more than 800,000 lines in the Fuchsia OS Zircon kernel.

Google has also come armed with a raft of benchmarks to back up its claims. On the software engineering DeepSWE v1.1 benchmark, Gemini 4 Argon hits 77.9 percent, which is higher than GPT-6 Astra, Fable 5.1, and Opus 5.5. Google promises similar power across a range of long-horizon tasks, pointing to Argon's industry-leading score in the economic analysis Vals Index test.

news.title: Google presenta Guided Vision: la nueva función de Gemini Live integrada en la cámara
news.summary: Google ha presentado Guided Vision, una nueva función de accesibilidad integrada en Gemini Live que permite a las personas ciegas y con baja visión obtener descripciones por voz de lo que capta la cámara del teléfono. La herramienta forma parte de las novedades de Android de septiembre de 2026 y ha sido desarrollada con la […] La entrada Google presenta Guided Vision: la nueva función de Gemini Live integrada en la cámara se publicó primero en Conticgo .
news.body:
Google ha presentado Guided Vision, una nueva función de accesibilidad integrada en Gemini Live que permite a las personas ciegas y con baja visión obtener descripciones por voz de lo que capta la cámara del teléfono.

La herramienta forma parte de las novedades de Android de septiembre de 2026 y ha sido desarrollada con la participación de las comunidades de personas ciegas y con baja visión.

Guided Vision es una función de Gemini Live que utiliza la cámara del teléfono para analizar lo que hay delante del usuario y ofrecer información mediante audio en tiempo real.

Por ejemplo, puede ayudar a leer textos pequeños, identificar objetos o comprender determinados elementos del entorno .

Google pone como ejemplos situaciones cotidianas como leer la letra pequeña de una etiqueta de alimentos, consultar un menú en un restaurante con poca iluminación o identificar objetos domésticos.

Una de sus características más interesantes es que no se limita a describir la imagen captada por la cámara. Si el teléfono no está correctamente orientado, Guided Vision puede proporcionar indicaciones por voz para reencuadrar la imagen, desplazar la cámara o centrar un objeto .

Según la documentación oficial de Google, Guided Vision puede utilizarse para diferentes tareas:

Esto permite utilizar la cámara del teléfono como una herramienta de apoyo para determinadas actividades cotidianas, sin necesidad de que el usuario tenga que interpretar visualmente toda la información que aparece en pantalla.

Google señala que Guided Vision ha sido diseñada para y junto a las comunidades de personas ciegas y con baja visión .

Además, la compañía ha integrado diferentes formas de acceso rápido. La función puede añadirse a los atajos de accesibilidad de Android y también puede utilizarse desde el menú de TalkBack , el lector de pantalla del sistema.

En los dispositivos compatibles, el acceso rápido puede configurarse mediante el botón de accesibilidad, un gesto o las teclas de volumen.

Para utilizar Guided Vision es necesario disponer de la aplicación móvil de Gemini y tener acceso a la función.

Desde los ajustes de Gemini se puede activar la opción «Usar Visión guiada en Live» . Después, al iniciar una conversación de Gemini Live, se comparte la cámara del teléfono para comenzar la sesión.

Google está realizando un despliegue progresivo , por lo que es posible que la función todavía no aparezca en todos los dispositivos o cuentas.

La compañía indica que Guided Vision está llegando a teléfonos con Android 9 o versiones posteriores , en los países donde Gemini está disponible.

Actualmente solo está disponible para esos modelos específicos de Android, su despliegue en el resto de dispositivos es prograsivo.

Aunque las posibilidades son interesantes para la accesibilidad, Google advierte de que Guided Vision puede cometer errores .

Por este motivo, la compañía especifica que no se trata de un dispositivo médico ni de una ayuda para la movilidad y que no debe utilizarse para navegar ni para detectar obstáculos .

Es especialmente importante tenerlo en cuenta cuando la herramienta describe un entorno o proporciona información sobre objetos: la respuesta de la inteligencia artificial debe considerarse una ayuda complementaria y no una garantía de que la información sea correcta.

La llegada de Guided Vision representa otro paso en la incorporación de la inteligencia artificial generativa a las herramientas de accesibilidad visual .

En este caso, la combinación de cámara, conversación por voz e inteligencia artificial permite plantear una interacción más natural: el usuario puede mostrar algo con el teléfono, preguntar qué está viendo y recibir una respuesta hablada.

Para las personas con baja visión, este tipo de herramientas puede resultar especialmente interesante en situaciones en las que la información visual es pequeña, está poco iluminada o resulta difícil de distinguir.

Eso sí, Guided Vision no sustituye a las ayudas ópticas, los productos de apoyo ni las herramientas de movilidad , sino que se plantea como una herramienta tecnológica adicional para determinadas tareas del día a día.

news.body:
Tal y como ha anunciado NV Access mediante esta publicación , la beta 3 de NVDA 2026.3 ya se encuentra disponible para descarga y pruebas. Si quieres saber qué ofrece la próxima versión de NVDA antes de que se libere oficialmente, no dudes en descargar esta beta y proporcionar comentarios por los canales de la comunidad, o por el sistema de informe de fallos de NV Access . Esta versión no es apta para entornos de producción. Al instalar esta beta te unirás al canal beta, y sólo recibirás avisos de actualización de compilaciones beta y candidatas a liberación (rc). El canal beta/rc siempre te mantendrá al día con la versión más reciente de NVDA. La última rc de un ciclo de liberación es idéntica a la última versión estable. Para regresar al canal de versiones estables, instala a mano la última versión estable.

Esta versión incorpora importantes mejoras de rendimiento, mejoras en los diálogos de NVDA, y entrada expandida por la pantalla táctil. Se han hecho varias mejoras para reducir los retrasos y aumentar el rendimiento. Ahora NVDA recupera y captura más información sobre los controles en segundo plano, mejorando el rendimiento en controles como cuadros combinados y el explorador de archivos. NVDA ya no hace que se rompan el explorador de archivos u otras aplicaciones al cerrarlo o reiniciarlo. NVDA se recupera ahora más rápido cuando una aplicación deja de responder, y ya no se colgará ni inundará el registro con errores en aplicaciones que no responden. En regiones vivas de texto, como las terminales, NVDA ya no se cuelga cuando se vuelcan en pantalla importantes cantidades de texto. Se han añadido menús de contexto y atajos de teclado a los diálogos de perfiles de configuración, gestos de entrada y diccionarios del habla, haciendo que estos diálogos sean más fáciles de usar con el teclado. Ahora también es posible cambiar directamente un gesto existente en el diálogo Gestos de entrada. Se ha modernizado el diálogo que presenta mensajes explorables y ahora soporta mejor cambiar su tamaño, maximizarlo y minimizarlo. Se ha expandido significativamente la entrada por pantalla táctil. Los gestos de dos deslizamientos secuenciales ahora combinan dos deslizamientos en rápida sucesión en un solo gesto, incrementando enormemente la cantidad de gestos asociables. También se soportan ahora los gestos de borde, permitiendo que los gestos que comiencen a 15 mm de cualquier borde de la pantalla se asocien independientemente de los mismos gestos realizados en el centro de la pantalla. Se ha añadido una nueva orden sin asignar para mover el cursor del ratón al centro de la vista ampliada. Se puede usar el OCR de Windows con la lupa o la cortina de pantalla activadas. Se ha actualizado Liblouis con nuevas tablas braille en Elfdaliano, sami, maorí, braille unificado inglés de Nueva Zelanda, y aitiano criollo, una tabla noruega para texto en español, y variantes adicionales de sueco de 6 y 8 puntos. Se ha actualizado Espeak NG añadiendo soporte para liguriano y abkhaz. Para instalar esta beta, puedes configurar el canal «rc y beta» en el complemento Selector del canal de actualización y buscar actualizaciones desde el menú Ayuda de NVDA, o actualizar desde una beta anterior. Y como siempre, también puedes descargar manualmente el instalador de NVDA 2026.3 beta 3 . Su suma de comprobación SHA256, que te permitirá garantizar la integridad del archivo descargado, es ca17ceb9cd3a8ed7b9732d2a6856c2c3979fbfd86fde1dad91a8a7170dcec612. ¡Feliz miércoles!

La entrada Ya disponible la tercera beta de NVDA 2026.3 se publicó primero en NVDA en español .

news.title: Announcing AnonyMouse's App Pick of the Month for September 2026: Restaurant Rush: Cook & Serve
news.summary: Welcome to the September 2026 installment of AnonyMouse's App Pick of the Month, where where each month I highlight a new or noteworthy app. This month's pick is Restaurant Rush: Cook & Serve . September 2026 has been one of those months where choosing just one App Pick of the Month has been especially difficult. It has felt like one of the busiest months I can remember on AppleVis, particularly when it comes to games. There have been so many new apps and games to check out, and several could easily have earned this month's spot. But after considering all the options, I kept coming back to Restaurant Rush. About Restaurant Rush Restaurant Rush is a restaurant simulation game that combines time management, strategy, and progression. You take customer orders, prepare food, serve customers (before their patience runs out), and earn coins that can be used to improve your establishments. As you progress, you can upgrade kitchen stations, add trays, hire waitstaff, unlock additional restaurants, and work your way through more than 50 recipes. Restaurant Rush includes a 100-day campaign as well as an Endless mode, so there is plenty to keep you busy. There are also daily missions and weekly challenges with global leaderboards. One thing I especially like is that there is always something else I want to accomplish. I might start out intending to play for just a few minutes, and before I know it, I've played several more rounds. Restaurant Rush is seriously addictive. For me, a big part of the appeal of Restaurant Rush is simply getting to play this type of game with VoiceOver. Cooking and restaurant management games are not a new genre, of course, but accessibility of these games has historically not been all that great. There is something really satisfying about finally getting to experience this style of game for myself, and accessibility is a priority for the app's developer. VoiceOver users get the same challenging experience as those with sight, with some thoughtful additions specific to making gameplay accessible. When VoiceOver is detected, the game can suggest accessibility settings, including a more relaxed pace that gives you additional time to react. But relaxed doesn't necessarily mean easy. Customers can still lose patience, orders still need to be prepared and delivered, and things can definitely get hectic. And that's actually part of what makes the game so much fun for me. I'm not looking for a game that plays itself just because it's accessible. I want something I can learn, get better at, and occasionally feel a little pressure while playing. Restaurant Rush gives me that feeling of wanting to try again, improve my score, earn more coins, make another upgrade, and see what happens next. Something else has made this month's App Pick especially enjoyable for me, and it goes beyond Restaurant Rush itself. Restaurant Rush has taken AppleVis by storm, and a big part of that is because of how the developer has gotten involved with the community. The developer of Restaurant Rush has been especially active in the discussion in the App Directory entry; players have reported accessibility issues, asked questions, and suggested improvements, and the developer has been responding directly to that feedback with enthusiastic engagement. This is truly wonderful to see, and I love it when a developer treats accessibility as an ongoing commitment, not a finished product. Why I’m Picking Restaurant Rush: Cook & Serve This Month This was not an easy month to choose just one app. September brought an impressive number of new additions to the AppleVis App Directory, especially games, and there were several that I seriously considered for this month's pick. Restaurant Rush ultimately won me over because it combines several things I enjoy: accessibility, strategy, progression, challenge, and, most importantly, fun. It's the kind of game where I tell myself I'm going to play one more round, only to discover that "one more round" somehow turned into several. I also like that Restaurant Rush is a style of game that hasn't always been readily accessible to VoiceOver users. There's something special about finally getting to enjoy a type of game that sighted players have been enjoying for years and being able to experience that same frantic fun for myself. If you enjoy casual games, cooking games, time-management games, or games where you gradually build and improve something, Restaurant Rush is certainly worth a look. Download the App Restaurant Rush: Cook & Serve is free to download from the App Store, with optional in-app purchases. It is designed for iPhone and requires iOS 15.0 or later. App Store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/restaurant-rush-cook-serve/id6773167802 Now It’s Your Turn Have you tried Restaurant Rush? Are you finding it as addictive as I am? What do you enjoy most about it, and what would you like to see added or improved in future updates? And considering how many interesting new apps and games appeared on AppleVis during September, I'm curious: what is your personal App Pick of the Month? Let me know in the comments. I always enjoy hearing what everyone else is playing, discovering, and enjoying.

news.title: Mobilio: la aplicación de inteligencia artificial que mejora la navegación de personas con baja visión
news.summary: La inteligencia artificial continúa abriendo nuevas posibilidades en el ámbito de la tiflotecnología. Un equipo de investigadores de la Universidad de Harvard ha desarrollado Mobilio, una aplicación para teléfonos inteligentes que busca mejorar la navegación de las personas ciegas y con baja visión mediante orientación continua, reconocimiento del entorno y detección de obstáculos. El proyecto, […] La entrada Mobilio: la aplicación de inteligencia artificial que mejora la navegación de personas con baja visión se publicó primero en Conticgo .
news.body:
La inteligencia artificial continúa abriendo nuevas posibilidades en el ámbito de la tiflotecnología. Un equipo de investigadores de la Universidad de Harvard ha desarrollado Mobilio , una aplicación para teléfonos inteligentes que busca mejorar la navegación de las personas ciegas y con baja visión mediante orientación continua, reconocimiento del entorno y detección de obstáculos.

El proyecto, presentado el 24 de agosto de 2026 por la Escuela de Ingeniería y Ciencias Aplicadas John A. Paulson de Harvard (SEAS), combina aprendizaje automático, información procedente de diferentes sensores y señales de audio personalizadas. Sus resultados iniciales se han publicado en la revista científica Nature Biomedical Engineering .

Mobilio ha sido diseñada para abordar algunas de las dificultades que pueden surgir durante los desplazamientos de personas ciegas o con baja visión. Entre sus objetivos se encuentran ofrecer indicaciones giro a giro, proporcionar orientación continua por caminos y aceras y detectar y evitar obstáculos.

Para ello, la aplicación utiliza distintos sensores integrados en el teléfono inteligente, como la cámara, el GPS y la unidad de medición inercial, que permite obtener información relacionada con el movimiento y la orientación del dispositivo. En los teléfonos que disponen de esta tecnología, también puede utilizar el sensor LiDAR.

Uno de los elementos destacados del proyecto es su sistema de visión artificial. Los investigadores han desarrollado un modelo entrenado con imágenes tomadas desde la perspectiva de una persona que camina, en lugar de depender exclusivamente de imágenes captadas desde vehículos. Esto permite trabajar en el reconocimiento de superficies relevantes para los desplazamientos a pie, como aceras, pasos de peatones y calzadas.

El objetivo es que el sistema pueda interpretar mejor el entorno de un peatón y ofrecer información útil para seguir una ruta.

A diferencia de los sistemas de navegación que se basan únicamente en instrucciones habladas, Mobilio emplea señales acústicas continuas en forma de pitidos .

Estos sonidos proceden de diferentes direcciones, como la izquierda o la derecha, y ayudan a indicar hacia dónde debe orientarse la persona. Además, el sistema adapta las señales en tiempo real a las características de cada usuario mediante un proceso de personalización.

Durante la marcha, la aplicación analiza cómo sigue la persona las indicaciones y ajusta los patrones y tonos de los sonidos para adaptarlos a sus necesidades. De esta forma, la propuesta de Harvard busca ofrecer una orientación más continua y personalizada, en lugar de limitarse a comunicar instrucciones puntuales.

Para evaluar Mobilio, el equipo de investigación realizó experimentos con 14 participantes , nueve personas ciegas y cinco con discapacidad visual, reclutadas a través del Carroll Center for the Blind, en Newton (Massachusetts).

Los participantes realizaron diferentes tareas de navegación utilizando un bastón blanco. Los resultados de Mobilio se compararon con una condición de referencia basada en Google Maps y el mismo tipo de bastón. Las pruebas incluyeron un recorrido exterior por una ruta planificada y un circuito interior con obstáculos que simulaban dificultades habituales del entorno.

Los resultados publicados fueron los siguientes:

Estos datos deben interpretarse dentro del contexto del estudio. Se trata de una investigación inicial con un grupo reducido de participantes y condiciones experimentales concretas. Los resultados no demuestran que Mobilio sea superior a todas las ayudas de movilidad ni garantizan el mismo rendimiento en cualquier entorno.

Además, el artículo científico señala que el tiempo de finalización del circuito de obstáculos aumentó aproximadamente un 17 % con Mobilio, un aspecto que también debe tenerse en cuenta al interpretar sus resultados.

Una de las características más relevantes del proyecto es su enfoque basado en el teléfono inteligente. En lugar de depender necesariamente de un dispositivo especializado diseñado exclusivamente para la navegación, los investigadores plantean utilizar sensores y capacidad de procesamiento que pueden encontrarse en un smartphone.

El equipo de Harvard explica que la intención es desarrollar una herramienta que pueda llegar a funcionar como una aplicación independiente y que, en el futuro, pueda distribuirse a través de una tienda de aplicaciones. Sin embargo, Mobilio todavía se encuentra en fase de investigación y desarrollo, por lo que no debe presentarse como una aplicación comercial disponible para su descarga .

Este enfoque puede resultar especialmente interesante desde la perspectiva de la accesibilidad, ya que plantea cómo aprovechar dispositivos de uso cotidiano para desarrollar nuevas herramientas de apoyo. No obstante, el acceso a un smartphone compatible, sus sensores y las condiciones de uso serán factores importantes para valorar su utilidad en la práctica.

Los investigadores tienen previsto continuar evaluando Mobilio en una mayor variedad de situaciones reales en el área de Boston. El objetivo es conocer mejor cómo se comporta el sistema en diferentes entornos y cómo puede integrarse en los hábitos cotidianos de las personas usuarias.

El equipo también trabaja en la evolución de la tecnología con el apoyo del Harvard Grid Accelerator, mientras que la Oficina de Desarrollo Tecnológico de Harvard ha protegido las innovaciones relacionadas con el proyecto y está explorando oportunidades de comercialización.

El desarrollo de Mobilio muestra una de las líneas de investigación actuales en tiflotecnología: la combinación de inteligencia artificial, sensores y sistemas de interacción adaptados a las necesidades de las personas con discapacidad visual.

Aunque todavía es necesario realizar más pruebas y evaluar su comportamiento en diferentes circunstancias, este proyecto contribuye al debate sobre cómo desarrollar herramientas que faciliten la movilidad y la autonomía.

Desde Conticgo, seguiremos atentos a los avances que permitan ampliar las opciones de accesibilidad y mejorar la experiencia de las personas ciegas y con baja visión.

Si te ha gustado esta noticia no te pierdas las últimas novedades en tiflotectnología en nuestro apartado de noticias y redes sociales .

Fuentes: Harvard , Nature .

news.title: Apple Releases Version 27.0.1 of iOS, iPadOS, and macOS with fix for Face ID on iPhone 18 Pro and More
news.summary: Apple has today released version 27.0.1 of iOS, iPadOS, and macOS, bringing assorted bug fixes, including for issues with Face ID on iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max. Apple has also released iOS 26.7.1, iPadOS 26.7.1, macOS Tahoe 26.7.1, and macOS Sequoia 15.8.1 for devices not running version 27 of their respective operating systems. As iOS 27.0.1, iPadOS 27.0.1, and macOS Golden Gate 27.0.1 were not distributed to external testers prior to their release, we do not have any information on whether they contain any accessibility fixes for blind, deaf blind, or low vision users at the time of writing. However, as these updates appear to have been released to address a small number of specific issues, we do not expect them to contain any such fixes. Release Notes iOS 27.0.1 This update provides bug fixes for your iPhone, including fixes for the following issues: iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max may unexpectedly restart when Face ID fails to authenticate A color artifact may appear on photos captured at 2x under certain lighting conditions at f/1.48 on a small number of iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max devices Opening Notification Center and Control Center simultaneously may cause the touchscreen to become unresponsive macOS Golden Gate 27.0.1 This update provides bug fixes for your Mac. How to Update iOS and iPadOS 27.0.1 are available via Over-the-Air Update (Settings > General > Software Update), via Finder on a Mac with macOS Catalina or later, or via iTunes on a PC or Mac with macOS Mojave or earlier. Before updating, we strongly recommend making a full and complete backup of your device (either locally or in iCloud, depending on personal preference). This will ensure that, in the unlikely event that something goes wrong during the update process, you will have a current backup on hand in case a device restore becomes necessary. Also, if using OTA update, we recommend plugging your device into a power source for the duration of the download/installation process, so as to prevent the unlikely event of your battery going dead during the update. To install macOS Golden Gate 27.0.1, choose System Settings from the Apple menu, select General in the table, click Software Update in the scroll area, and click the Update Now button to begin the update process. If other updates are available, you can click the Info button to see details about them and select specific updates to install.
