news.title: In-Process 28th September 2026
news.summary: Let’s talk about NVDA 2026.3! NVDA 2026.3 Beta 2 Changes to the Changes Our International Communities Copying last spoken text Talking about NVDA Show Screen Overview NVDA 2026.3 Beta 2 As mentioned last edition, we released NVDA 2026.2 and dived straight into the beta period for NVDA 2026.3. Firstly, do go back and read all… Read More
news.body:
Let’s talk about NVDA 2026.3!

As mentioned last edition, we released NVDA 2026.2 and dived straight into the beta period for NVDA 2026.3 . Firstly, do go back and read all about NVDA 2026.2 if needed, but otherwise, let’s dive into what is coming up in NVDA 2026.3:

This release includes significant performance improvements, improvements to NVDA’s dialogs, and expanded touch screen input.

Several performance improvements have been made to reduce lag and improve responsiveness. NVDA now fetches and caches more information about controls in the background, improving performance in controls such as combo boxes and File Explorer. NVDA no longer causes File Explorer or other applications to crash when NVDA is exited or restarted. NVDA now recovers more quickly when an application stops responding, and will no longer freeze or flood the log with errors from unresponsive applications. In live text regions, such as terminals, NVDA no longer freezes when substantial amounts of text are dumped to the screen.

Context menus and keyboard shortcuts have been added to the Configuration Profiles, Input Gestures, and Speech Dictionaries dialogs, making these dialogs easier to use with the keyboard. It is also now possible to change an existing gesture directly in the Input Gestures dialog. The dialog used to present browsable messages has been modernized and now better supports resizing, maximizing, and minimizing.

Touch screen input has been significantly expanded. Sequential two-flick gestures now combine two flicks in quick succession into a single gesture, greatly increasing the number of bindable touch gestures. Edge gestures are also now supported, allowing gestures that begin within 15 mm of any screen edge to be bound independently from the same gesture performed in the centre of the screen.

A new unassigned command has been added to move the mouse cursor to the centre of the magnified view. Windows OCR can now be used while the Screen Curtain or NVDA’s built-in Magnifier is active.

Liblouis has been updated with new Elfdalian, Sami, Maori, New Zealand Unified English Braille, and Haitian Creole braille tables, a Norwegian table for Spanish text, and additional Swedish 6 and 8 dot variants. eSpeak NG has been updated with added support for Ligurian and Abkhaz.

Updates to translations Fix bug with Magnifier’s “Show screen overview” feature when using relative tracking mode Updated eSpeak In browse mode, alt+upArrow and alt+downArrow now collapse or expand combo boxes in more situations Prevent flashing from shifting magnifier colour filters to reduce seizure risk Update to the Chinese Word Segmentation library cppjieba to fix startup crashes from Chinese paths

If you’ve looked at the changes document for the NVDA 2026.3 betas , you might have noticed a change to the formatting. Or rather, some new formatting. Instead of having a list of features, and then breaking that up into sub-lists of Braille features and Touch Screen features and Browse mode features, we’ve made them headings:

“What’s new in NVDA” is at the top of the document and is a heading level 1 – press shift+1 to jump back to that from anywhere (or control+home since it’s at the top of the document). The version of NVDA, “2026.3”, “2026.2” etc, is a heading level 2. Press 2 to jump to the next older version of NVDA, or shift+2 to jump back to the start of the current version, or next newest version of NVDA. “New features”, “Changes”, “Bug Fixes”, “Changes for Developers”, “Security fixes”, and “Important notes” are all Heading level 3. sub-headings in the section, new features, changes, etc, are heading level 4. In the “New Features” for NVDA 2026.3 for instance, press 4 to jump to “Braille”, “Touch Screen Input”, “Browse Mode”, which are all sections of new features for this version.

If you are used to simply arrowing down through the list and reading each feature, that still works as it did. Or if you press i to jump between list items, that will still work, although you will miss the heading. If you navigate like that and hear “List with x items” and you’re not sure what the list is, press shift+h to jump to the previous heading (at any level) and it will move to the heading just before the list. As something new, we’re interested in what you think – good or bad. It’s the first time we’ve changed the formatting in awhile (though not the first at all, though the last change will not have been as noticeable to all our users).

While we’ve been sprucing things up, we recently gave the “ Connect with the NVDA Community ” page a once over. Firstly, we made sure all the links worked and followed up those with problems. As a result of that, we’ve removed a couple in consultation with their owners (Finnish and Swedish particularly) and added a couple more we had found along the way (Hi to our friends from the Brazilian Portuguese site!)

We also took the opportunity to add headings at H3 for each language, so you can jump or link to the Romanian resources directly now.

We’re always interested in adding new resources to the list. Are you aware of any other groups we’re not aware of? Particularly in languages not yet listed there. Please get in touch if you know of any.

One of the popular features in NVDA 2026.2 was the addition of NVDA+x to repeat the last spoken information. You could press that twice quickly to have the information displayed in a dialog so you could read it with more granular control. If what you want to do is copy the information, while you can do it from that dialog, we’ve added a new command to NVDA 2026.3 to make it even easier. Press NVDA+control+x to copy the last spoken information directly to the clipboard. Thank you to community contributor Cary for his work on this feature!

(A screenshot of the original NVDA+x double press dialog, showing the new feature bullet point for the NVDA+control+x command. Note the dialog has white text on black, because I had the magnifier running with colours inverted when I took the screenshot.)

We love talking about NVDA! I often forget to mention interviews here, but we’ve recently done a couple I thought I’d share:

Access Point Firstly, our “Access Point” collaboration with World Services for the Blind continues with the second in our podcast series, on everything new in NVDA 2026.2.

Tek Talk Next, Training & Support Manager Quentin was on Tek Talk , again covering everything new with NVDA.

And, on a slightly different topic NOT involving us talking – but if YOU love talking about NVDA, accessibility and navigation, Monash University, in Australia, are offering a paid PhD Scholarship in Communication and Navigation for Blind and Low Vision People .

Monash are looking for a linguist or researcher with a related background to investigate how Blind and Low Vision people navigate the world using technology.

The project focuses on video ethnography, multimodal communication, and users’ experiences of navigation technology, with opportunities to collaborate with researchers in assistive technology and AI.

This is open to both Australians and International applicants It’s also part of the Monash Assistive Technology and Society Centre (MATS) and Monash AI Institute so the successful applicant will have lots of opportunity to collaborate with technologists about building better navigational tech going forward.

Do refer to the position description at Monash for all the details.

One of the features of the magnifier we didn’t mention much last time is the Show Entire Screen Overview. Since one of the fixes in the latest NVDA 2026.3 beta is a fix involving this feature, I thought it was worth a mention. So firstly, the fix is that it WILL now work if using relative tracking mode – so if you prefer that magnifier tracking mode, you might want to upgrade before trying it out.

With the magnifier running, press NVDA+shift+L to “Show entire screen”. This temporarily zooms out to show the whole screen (as if the magnifier wasn’t running). After a couple of seconds without the mouse moving, the view zooms back in again.

Because the view smoothly zooms out and then back in again, it makes it easier to tell where the zoomed area is in relation to the whole screen. By waiting for mouse movement to stop, it allows a user to explore the unmagnified view and then smoothly zooms in to where the focus currently is.

If you wish to instantly enable or disable the magnifier, NVDA+shift+w will do this immediately, without zoom out (and then only magnifies again once you press NVDA+shift+w again).

Another difference is that pressing NVDA+shift+L zooms out but leaves any colour filtering enabled. If you wish to quickly zoom out and remove colour filtering, then you may find turning off the magnifier ( NVDA+shift+w ) works better.

And a related tip – if you don’t want magnification BUT do want colour filtering, you can enable the magnifier, enable colour filtering ( NVDA+shift+i ) and then zoom out to 1x ( NVDA+shift+minus ).

That’s all for this week. A little longer than it sometimes is, but there we covered quite a few keystrokes – did you learn any new ones? Surely at least NVDA+control+x ? Do try out the latest 2026.3 beta, and some of those commands. Do please keep giving feedback on the changes and improvements. Also please do share any other international communities we aren’t yet aware of.

news.title: Kodou - Swipe & Connect
news.summary: Kodou is a swipe-to-connect puzzle where every board plays a little differently and the clock never stops. Drag your finger across matching tiles, or find an ascending run of powers of two, 2 to 4 to 8 to 16 and beyond, for a bigger payoff. HOW TO PLAY - Swipe to connect three or more tiles: match the same value, or chain an ascending sequence of powers of two for double the score. - Watch for special tiles. Wildcards match any value, Ice tiles freeze your clock when cleared, and Bombs clear the block around them. - Plan around Blockers. They cannot be chained through. - The turn timer speeds up the longer you survive, so think fast and keep your eyes on the board. FEATURES - A twelve color palette that adapts to light and dark mode, so no two boards ever look quite the same. - Game Center leaderboards for both Score and Longest Chain, with All Time, Weekly, and Daily standings. - Full VoiceOver support. Explore the board by touch, then drag to connect a chain exactly the way a sighted player would, or build one tap at a time if you prefer. - Play the exact same game on Apple Watch. Kodou is free to play, supported by ads. A one time Remove Ads purchase clears all of them for good.

news.title: Restaurant Rush: Cook & Serve
news.summary: Cook fast, serve happy guests and decorate your own restaurant. Cozy chaos, two cats to pet, and fully playable with VoiceOver. Open your doors and start your shift! Restaurant Rush: Cook & Serve is a fast, cozy restaurant time-management game. Orders pile up, guests get impatient, and you keep the kitchen running one shift at a time. Play your way • Run 5 restaurants, each with its own menu and levels. Start at Sip Stop and work your way up. • Story levels for steady progress, or Endless Shift, where you pick draft cards to shape every run. • Unlock recipes and kitchen upgrades with Dollars, and hire a waiter for the busy rushes. • Finish daily goals and climb the leaderboards. • How to Play: a short guide on the main menu explains the game modes, pace, combos and the screen layout. • Practice: quick lessons and a free practice shift where nobody leaves. Make it yours • Restaurant Studio: decorate with themes, wall decorations, counters and tables. • Spend Coins on chef outfits, music tracks, soundscapes and accessories for the cats. Meet Holosko and Sabri • Two cats live in your restaurant. Pet them to calm down impatient guests. Hear the restaurant come alive • Realistic kitchen and customer sounds: the door, footsteps, chairs, pouring and cooking. Play at your own pace • Fully playable with VoiceOver. • Accessible play and pace settings, including Relaxed, so anyone can play at their own speed. • Left-handed layout. • Available in 9 languages. Tie your apron and open the doors. Your first guests are already waiting.
news.body:
Welcome to Restaurant Rush — the cozy kitchen-builder where every shift is a tiny puzzle.

Run five themed restaurants across a 100-day story campaign, then push your record in Endless mode. Drag ingredients to the stove, plate orders before the timer ticks out, and bank coins to expand your menu, hire a waiter, or unlock the next neighborhood spot.

What you'll do

• Serve thirsty customers at Sip Stop, plate noodle bowls at Noodle Pit, toss tacos at Taco Truck, and three more restaurants to discover.

• Master the rhythm: tap to take orders, prep at the right station, deliver before patience runs out, chase combos for huge tips.

• Upgrade kitchen stations, add trays, hire waiters per restaurant, and unlock 50+ recipes that scale with your skill.

• Customize your chef with 8 outfit presets, 4 hair styles, and a wardrobe of premium cosmetic items you unlock as you progress.

Live ops that respect your time

• Daily missions reset at midnight with shareable rewards. • Weekly challenges with global leaderboards. • Seasonal content drops curated by the live-ops team — new recipes, customer types, and chef gear show up without you needing to update the app.

Built for one-handed play

Restaurant Rush is designed for short sessions on the bus, in line, or before bed. No timers gating progress, no energy meter to wait out — just keep cooking when you want, pause anywhere.

Free to download. Optional in-app purchases support continued development.

news.title: Tact es una nueva herramienta utiliza IA para crear cuentos en Braille con ilustraciones táctiles
news.summary: La inteligencia artificial también está comenzando a explorar nuevas formas de crear materiales accesibles. Un ejemplo reciente es Tact, un proyecto que combina inteligencia artificial, Braille e impresión 3D para generar cuentos infantiles acompañados de ilustraciones táctiles. El sistema, presentado por el investigador Iliano Fasolino, permite introducir una idea para una historia, incluso mediante voz, […] La entrada Tact es una nueva herramienta utiliza IA para crear cuentos en Braille con ilustraciones táctiles se publicó primero en Conticgo .
news.body:
La inteligencia artificial también está comenzando a explorar nuevas formas de crear materiales accesibles. Un ejemplo reciente es Tact , un proyecto que combina inteligencia artificial, Braille e impresión 3D para generar cuentos infantiles acompañados de ilustraciones táctiles.

El sistema, presentado por el investigador Iliano Fasolino, permite introducir una idea para una historia, incluso mediante voz, y generar una página preparada para su impresión con texto en Braille e ilustraciones en relieve . El proyecto está pensado principalmente para niños ciegos y con baja visión de aproximadamente 4 a 10 años.

Tact es un sistema basado en navegador que permite crear pequeños cuentos táctiles a partir de una idea introducida por el usuario. Esta propuesta puede escribirse o incluso dictarse mediante voz.

A partir de ella, el sistema genera una historia y prepara una página que combina texto en Braille e ilustraciones en relieve .

El proyecto está pensado principalmente para niños de entre 4 y 10 años y pretende facilitar que familiares, docentes y profesionales puedan crear materiales personalizados sin necesidad de conocimientos especializados en diseño táctil.

Uno de los aspectos más interesantes de Tact es que no convierte directamente una imagen convencional en un relieve.

El sistema utiliza una biblioteca de formas táctiles previamente diseñadas. Según explica su autor, actualmente incluye 93 formas relacionadas con animales, objetos, naturaleza y otros elementos habituales en los cuentos infantiles.

La inteligencia artificial selecciona las formas necesarias para representar determinadas escenas y las organiza junto al texto.

Este planteamiento es especialmente relevante porque una ilustración diseñada para verse no siempre funciona cuando se explora mediante el tacto. Las formas deben ser sencillas y estar suficientemente separadas para facilitar su identificación.

Una vez generado el contenido, Tact prepara un archivo STL , que puede utilizarse para fabricar la página mediante una impresora 3D.

El proyecto utiliza como referencia la norma ISO 17049:2013 para las características del Braille.

De esta manera, el proceso intenta reunir en una misma herramienta varias tareas: crear la historia, convertir el texto a Braille, seleccionar las formas táctiles y preparar el archivo necesario para su fabricación.

Actualmente, el sistema permite generar historias en inglés e italiano , por lo que todavía no ofrece generación directa en español.

La posibilidad de crear cuentos personalizados puede ser especialmente interesante en el ámbito educativo.

Un docente o una familia podría generar una historia adaptada a los intereses de un niño y acompañarla de una representación táctil relacionada con el contenido.

Esto podría contribuir a ampliar la disponibilidad de materiales accesibles, especialmente aquellos que son demasiado específicos o personalizados como para encontrarlos fácilmente en un catálogo de libros adaptados.

Además, el proyecto apuesta por tecnologías relativamente accesibles, como una impresora 3D, para facilitar la fabricación de los materiales.

Aunque Tact plantea una propuesta interesante, todavía se encuentra en una fase de desarrollo.

El propio autor señala que es necesario realizar más trabajo y validar el sistema directamente con personas ciegas y con sordoceguera y con las organizaciones que las representan .

Esta validación será fundamental para comprobar que las ilustraciones generadas son realmente fáciles de interpretar mediante el tacto y que el diseño de las páginas resulta adecuado para los usuarios.

Por tanto, Tact no debe considerarse todavía una solución educativa plenamente validada, sino una propuesta de investigación que explora cómo la inteligencia artificial puede facilitar la creación de materiales táctiles.

Tact muestra una de las posibles líneas de evolución de la tecnología accesible: utilizar la inteligencia artificial no solo para describir imágenes o reconocer textos, sino también para crear nuevos recursos accesibles desde cero .

La combinación de IA, Braille e impresión 3D podría facilitar en el futuro la creación de materiales personalizados para personas ciegas y con baja visión.

El proyecto todavía tiene retos por delante, pero plantea una posibilidad interesante: que crear determinados materiales táctiles personalizados pueda ser mucho más sencillo y accesible para familias, docentes y entidades.

news.title: Apple Releases watchOS 27.0.1 with fix for unexpected restarts on Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4
news.summary: Apple has today released watchOS 27.0.1 for Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4, bringing a fix for an issue that caused the devices to restart unexpectedly. As watchOS 27.0.1 was not distributed to external testers prior to its release, we do not have any information on whether it contains any accessibility fixes for blind, deaf blind, or low vision users at the time of writing. However, as this update appears to have been released to address a specific issue on a small subset of devices, we do not expect it to contain any such fixes. watchOS 27.0.1 Release Notes (via 9to5Mac ) This update provides bug fixes for your Apple Watch including fixing an issue where Apple Watch may restart unexpectedly. How to Update watchOS 27.0.1 is available via Over-the-Air Update (Settings > General > Software Update) or by going to the Watch app on your iPhone and navigating to General > Software Update. To install the update, your Watch must be connected to its charger and have at least 50% battery power.
news.body:

This update provides bug fixes for your Apple Watch including fixing an issue where Apple Watch may restart unexpectedly.

news.title: Scratch Mancer: Card Roguelike
news.summary: A scratch-card roguelike. You work the night counter of a House that sells luck sealed under foil. The quota is due by dawn. Miss it, and the House keeps you. Every ticket is a grid of foil hiding cash, multipliers and skulls. Your thumb is the budget — stamina runs out long before the tickets do, so where you scratch matters as much as what's under it. THE DECISION YOU MAKE ALL GAME • Scratch a cell to 20% and you can read the fragment — it doesn't count and it doesn't trigger • Scratch to 45% and it counts for real, skulls included • One revealed skull halves the payout. Two void the ticket • Cash out whenever you like. Only what you revealed pays BUILD A RUN THAT BENDS THE ODDS • 40 charms across 5 slots: reroll skulls into coins, drift sevens toward corners, make a graze count as a hit • A warden calls every third night. Each one bends a rule you were leaning on. There are six of them • Seven ticket types, each with its own payout rule — match three, complete a crossword, climb a rising ladder, or reveal a single cell on an Offering and stop • Four single-use tools in three pockets: spray the foil to see straight through it, magnet a symbol sideways, sticker a skull into a seven • Nine nights, each with a quota due at dawn. Then endless, if you're still standing • Beat the House and the Seals open: seven stacked terms for the players who won, one added per win. Higher quotas, a skull on every ticket, wardens arriving early, two on the last night. Break all seven NO ADS. NO PAYWALLS. JUST SCRATCHING. One purchase, the whole game. The odds don't know what you paid, because there is no second payment to make: no coins to buy, no subscription, no season pass, no timers. • Plays fully offline • Family Sharing enabled • Game Center achievements and leaderboards • One thumb, portrait, a night finishes on a bus ride • Built for iPhone and iPad by one developer Scratch the foil, read what you can, and try to leave before the House notices. Scratchmancer is a work of fiction. No real money changes hands, no real lottery products appear, and the odds in it are invented.
